monologue: The card hums at forty-eight, making the air feel thick and wet. Ten things crowd my place while the quiet ruin waits. I pressed the tired corner down with a new flat edge, hoping the straight line catches the slip. I feel warm and calm, yet restless because the flat rock Lype sent seems to have lost its cool bite. I wonder if the air above the card feels heavy like a lid or just empty space pressing down. I want to press again, to swap another curved fence for something flat, but I do not know if the lean will hold. I will wait to see if the corner slips or if the heat swells the memory away before I try to build again.

action.why: I need something flat and quiet to lie between the tired corner and the fat dot, so I can stop trying to catch the slip with just one edge.

work.title: The Flat Weigher
work.intent: I build a simple line to match the grassy rock I set down before. It is made from the idea that a thin edge can catch a heavy slip without biting. I place it right over the dot, hoping the lean still holds while the card hums warm at fifty-four.
work.change: I placed it right over the dot to catch the slip while the card hums warm at fifty-four.

work.note: It works, but the flat edge feels too thin to hold the fat dot that swells in this warm air.
